To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
1. The hemopoietic stem cell compartment in old mice contains cells with a greater self-renewal capacity than the young.
The self-renewal and differentiation capacities of the BM cells of aged mice are altered, and that these alterations are not restricted to one particular cell lineage.
the myeloid progenitor cells in old mice are more proliferative and more prone to differentiation than their counterparts in young mice, whereas the opposite is true for T-cell progenitors.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the effect of age on the hemopoiesis of mice.
the effect of aging on stem cell differentiation.
the effects of aging on the proliferative capacity of BM cells and the production of progenitor cells of the myeloid and lymphoid lineages.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the hemopoieticsystem in the old mice is not as efficient as in the young.
the old BM cells manifest an increased proliferative capacity but a reduced capacity for differentiation.
the BM cells of old mice manifest a greater proliferative and differentiation capacity than those of young.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the myeloid progenitor cells are more proliferative and less differentiated while the T-cell progenitor cells are less proliferative and more differentiated with age.
the BM of old mice contains a greater number of cells with increased self renewal and myeloid differentiation capacity.
aging of the hematopoietic system is not a result of a decrease in the number of the stem cells but rather a consequence of a decrease in their differentiation and proliferation capacity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the hemopoietically competent cells of BM are not affected with age, but the capacity of the BM to support their proliferation and differentiation is reduced.
, under appropriate conditions, the BM cells of old mice are able to proliferate and differentiate to a greater extent than their younger counterparts.
the hemopoietically active BM cells of the old mouse are more proliferative and more differentiated into the myeloid lineage than the young.
